# Alert Discord when a high-priority Jira issue is created

**Pattern:** Event -> filter -> alert · **Level:** Production · **Trigger:** Jira webhook

## What it does
Posts a Discord alert only for newly created High and Highest priority Jira issues, dropping everything below the bar.

## Why it exists
An alert channel is only useful if it stays quiet for routine work. This filters the issue firehose down to the ones worth interrupting for, and pushes those into chat the moment they're filed.

## Main flow
Jira Issue Created -> Extract Issue Fields -> Keep High & Highest -> Format Alert -> Post to Discord (failure -> error rail).

## Use it for
- An on-call channel that should only hear urgent issues
- Escalating Sev-1/Sev-2 bugs the moment they're filed
- A high-signal feed separate from the full firehose

## You get
- Only High/Highest alert — no routine noise
- Per-issue alerts, automatically
- Alerts that name the owner and link the issue

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Jira API token; Discord webhook URL.
Colour key: 🟦 entry · 🟫 app I/O · ⬜ logic · 🟩 output · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
This is event-driven; sample events (High, Highest, and a Low to be filtered) are pinned so you can test the Filter with no credential. Sample data is pinned on the trigger, so hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow end to end before attaching a single credential. Right-click → Unpin when you go live.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never bundled in a template. Every node that talks to an external service needs its own connection before the first real run — open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Jira API token**
Atlassian → account settings → Security → API tokens → Create. n8n's Jira SW Cloud credential takes your account email, the token, and your site URL (https://your-domain.atlassian.net).
_Gotcha:_ The token inherits your Jira permissions — it can only read/write projects your own account can access.

**Discord webhook URL**
Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook → Copy Webhook URL. Paste it into n8n's Discord Webhook credential.
_Gotcha:_ A webhook URL is bound to one channel. Use a separate webhook/credential per channel you post to.

Set each credential up once; it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Nothing happens when the event should fire**
Cause: The workflow is still a draft, or its trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate it. The manual test URL is different from the production URL.

**A node shows a red triangle right after import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials note).

**Nothing ever alerts**
Cause: Your Jira priorities are named differently (e.g. P1/P2), so the Filter never matches.
Fix: The Filter matches the literal names High/Highest. Edit them to whatever your Jira scheme calls its top priorities.

**Medium issues slip through**
Cause: A third condition was added, or the combinator was changed.
Fix: Keep it to two OR conditions: priority equals High, or equals Highest.

**Discord posts nothing / returns 400**
Cause: The message content resolved to an empty string, or the webhook URL is wrong.
Fix: Discord rejects empty content. Check the upstream expression produced text, and re-copy the webhook URL.

Still stuck? The **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there.

## Design decisions

The priority names are matched literally because Jira priority schemes are per-instance — there is no universal enum — so this is the one line you're expected to tune. There's no Loop node: the Discord node runs once per item, so the Filter's output is the fan-out. Subscribing only to issue_created (not updated) keeps the alert about *new* urgent work, not every edit to an old ticket.

## Practice exercises

Already production-shaped — deepen it:

1. Add issue_updated and alert when any issue is *raised* to High/Highest.
2. @mention the on-call role for Highest only, and just post for High.
3. Route by project so different teams' urgent issues hit different channels.

## 🛠 Customize me

The priority bar is in **Keep High & Highest** — edit the literal names to match your Jira scheme (e.g. `P1`/`P2`). Add `issue_updated` to also catch issues *raised* to high priority. @mention on-call for Highest only by splitting the Format branch.

## 🔐 Security

Scope the Jira token to the project(s) you watch. Urgent-issue summaries reach Discord fast — route them to the on-call channel and keep it private. The Discord webhook URL lives in the credential only.
